claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the Provider support policy page) that the support index links to.
The Provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Some Pulumi providers get long-term security updates under the Pulumi provider support policy, while others do not.
Pulumi's provider version support policy focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers Pulumi maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi also ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The Pulumi provider support policy page lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers (beyond the latest major and, for covered providers, the previous major) receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry lets you find the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
The page /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists as a link target.
Using the tilde operator in npm (~1.2.3) allows patch updates on the current minor version.

Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic to smooth the upgrade from the immediately previous major version, but these migrations do not always work across multiple major versions.
Experimental Pulumi features are always opt-in, enabled with a flag, command, or environment variable such as PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection, and `pulumi up --refresh` refreshes and applies in a single step.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version (N−1) for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers that receive long-term support updates on eligible older versions are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
Registry package pages exist at /registry/packages/aws/, azure/, azure-native/, azuread/, command/, docker-build/, gcp/, kubernetes/, tls/, and vault/.
The Pulumi provider LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches, including fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or its direct dependencies.
The Pulumi provider LTS branch ships fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship the security patches.

A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
LTS provider releases remain compatible with the version of Pulumi they were frozen at, unless security fixes require otherwise.
Under the Pulumi provider support policy, exactly one long-term support major version exists per provider at any time.

When major version N+1 of a covered provider ships, it becomes the new N, the old N becomes the new LTS major, and the old LTS major reaches end of life the same day regardless of how much of its 12-month window remained.
Within the LTS major version of a covered provider, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
Pulumi provider LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version of a covered provider (the recommended approach) automatically receive patch releases as they ship.
At any time exactly one major version of a covered provider is the LTS version, and older majors receive no patches.
If v3 is the newest release, v3 is N, v2 is N−1, and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major (N) of a Pulumi provider receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
The long-term support phase (N−1) provides security updates in the provider's code or its direct dependencies for up to 12 months from N's release, or until N+1 ships.
End-of-life provider versions (N−2 and older) are not supported and receive no updates.
The Pulumi support FAQ at /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ has an entry titled 'What are the best practices for maintaining provider versions'.
Pages exist at /registry/ and /docs/support/getting-support/.
